The '''61st [[Golden Globe Award]]s''', honoring the best in [[film]] and television for 2003, were held on January 25, 2004, at the [[Beverly Hilton Hotel]] in [[Beverly Hills]], [[California]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Hayes|first1=Dade|title=By Gollum, it’s ‘The King’|url=https://variety.com/2004/film/awards/by-gollum-it-s-the-king-1117899023/|access-date=10 January 2018|work=Variety|date=25 January 2004|archive-date=January 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180111164947/http://variety.com/2004/film/awards/by-gollum-it-s-the-king-1117899023/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title='Return of the King' dominates Golden Globes|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2004/SHOWBIZ/Movies/01/25/golden.globes/|access-date=10 January 2018|work=CNN|date=26 January 2004|archive-date=January 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190121121841/http://edition.cnn.com/2004/SHOWBIZ/Movies/01/25/golden.globes/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Welkos|first1=Robert|last2=King|first2=Susan|title=Gold rush is on|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2004-jan-26-et-welkos26-story.html|access-date=10 January 2018|work=Los Angeles Times|date=26 January 2004|archive-date=December 16, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241216035432/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2004-jan-26-et-welkos26-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The nominations were announced on December 18, 2003.<ref>{{cite news|title=Globes high on 'Cold Mountain'|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2003/SHOWBIZ/Movies/12/18/globe.noms/index.html|access-date=10 January 2018|work=CNN|date=18 December 2003|archive-date=February 2, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202031938/http://edition.cnn.com/2003/SHOWBIZ/Movies/12/18/globe.noms/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Welkos|first1=Robert|last2=King|first2=Susan|title='Cold' call from Globes|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2003-dec-19-et-globes19-story.html|access-date=10 January 2018|work=Los Angeles Times|date=19 December 2003|archive-date=June 26, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240626110023/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2003-dec-19-et-globes19-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=And the nominees are...|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2003-dec-19-et-globelist19-story.html|access-date=10 January 2018|work=Los Angeles Times|date=19 December 2003|archive-date=December 13, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213085519/https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2003-dec-19-et-globelist19-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

''[[The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King]]'' won the most awards, with 4 (including Best Motion Picture – Drama). ''[[Cold Mountain (film)|Cold Mountain]]'' received the most nominations, with 8 (winning 1, Best Supporting Actress). ''[[Big Fish]]'' had the most nominations (4) without a single win.

The ceremony was watched by a record-setting audience of 26.8 million people.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jamshowbiz.com/TelevisionRatings/us.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040203065228/http://www.jamshowbiz.com/TelevisionRatings/us.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2004-02-03|title=Golden Globes set NBC ratings record|date=January 28, 2004|publisher=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>
